en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty Ninth Chapter
The Discourse on the Sound of the Emanation of Thought:
Is it the case that for one who is entirely engaged in thought and sustained application, there is a sound produced by the emanation of thought?

Is it that for one who contacts in every way, sound is the diffusion of contact; for one who feels in every way, sound is the diffusion of feeling; for one who perceives in every way, sound is the diffusion of perception;
for one who intends in every way, sound is the diffusion of volition; for one who thinks in every way, sound is the diffusion of consciousness;
for one who remembers in every way, sound is the diffusion of mindfulness; and for one who understands in every way, sound is the diffusion of wisdom?
It should not be said so … [as before] … When one is entirely engaged in applied thought (*vitakka*) and sustained thought (*vicāra*), is sound the result of the diffusion of applied thought? Yes.
“Is it not the case that the sound produced by the movement of thought (vitakkavipphāra) is cognizable by the ear, strikes against the ear, and comes within the range of the ear?

… [as before] … “Is it not the case, then, that the sound produced by the movement of thought is not cognizable by the ear, does not strike against the ear, and does not come within the range of the ear?”

“If the sound produced by the diffusion of applied thought (vitakkavipphāra) is not cognizable by the ear, does not strike the ear, and does not come within the range of the ear, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
‘The sound produced by the diffusion of applied thought belongs to one who is entirely engaged in applied thought and sustained thought.’”
The Discussion on the Sound of the Emanation of Thought is finished.
